findings.element: The loading skeleton — .sk-wrap (lately.html:486-487, plus the neutralising pass at lately.html:1195-1204), at ?state=loading
findings.problem: Round 2 neutralised every magnitude that carries geometry — --h, --f, --x, the .part treatment, the .zero class and the record tag — but left every fact in the DOM as live text, hidden only by `color: transparent`. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 on ?v=light&state=loading&motion=settled, a real Ctrl+A selects and paints the whole unread reading: 31, +5 ON THE FOUR BEFORE, 'jobs finished, Harbour House weddings — this week still running', the gridline values 6 and 12, 12 SO FAR, five week ticks, OPEN NOW 9, jobs not finished, 3 / 2 / 1 / 0 with all four of their sentences, and OLDEST · 41 DAYS. document.querySelector('.sk-wrap').innerText returns the same reading in full. The six assertions in the block headed 'a state that says it is still reading may not publish the reading' (interaction-check.mjs:1441-1446) read --h, --f, --x, two class names and one visibility; not one of them reads text, so the gate is green over this and the round-2 note records the leak as closed.
findings.consequence: The loading state's only claim is that these numbers have not been read yet, and one ordinary keystroke displays them in full, at full value, in the exact positions they will occupy. They are not necessarily the numbers that arrive: on this same fixture the partial reading resolves the overdue card to 'not available', not to the 2 the selection shows. A person who selects, copies or runs find-in-page while the surface is loading is handed a reading the product has not made — the fabricated-figure class the honest-degradation contract exists to forbid, reached through a different door. I stopped short of misleading only because nothing is put in front of a passive reader.
findings.fix: Add `-webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none;` to the .sk-wrap rule at lately.html:486, beside the `pointer-events: none` that is already there for the same reason. Measured: Ctrl+A on ?state=loading then returns the header, 'Loading this reading.' and the refusals movement and nothing else, and no box moves, because selection does not affect layout. (I tested replacing digits with U+2007 instead: it is a whitespace character, it collapses against neighbouring spaces, and it moved the hero box 7.6px. Do not use it.)
findings.assertion: On ?state=loading, press Control+A and assert window.getSelection().toString() matches none of /\b31\b/, /41 days/i, /12 so far/i or /Open now/i, and carries no digit that appears inside .sk-wrap; and assert getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.sk-wrap')).userSelect === 'none'. Prove it can fail by removing the declaration and watching the selection come back.

findings.element: interaction-check.mjs:513 — ok("settled means every column is already at its height", still.h > 8) — reading a page returned by open() (interaction-check.mjs:76-77), which waits 1800ms before it hands the page back
findings.problem: The entrance is over long before the measurement is taken. The columns run 0.5s on a delay of i*40ms + 340ms, so the last of the twelve finishes at 1280ms; the check happens at 1800ms. Driven both ways at 1440x960: ?state=full&v=light (data-motion is 'settled') gives a first column of 70.55px at 1800ms, and ?state=full&v=light&motion=play — settled explicitly switched off — gives 70.55px at the same instant. Sampled earlier with motion=play the same column measures 0.00px at 0ms and at 200ms, 32.83px at 400ms (already past the 8px threshold) and 70.55px at 800ms. The assertion therefore returns the same true whether or not [data-motion="settled"] is honoured at all; the only way it can fail is a column whose own data height is under 8px, which is not what it is named for. Every frame in shots/ and every reproducibility claim in this lab rests on the settled override, and nothing in 461 assertions watches it work.
findings.consequence: The motion contract is an untested claim, and it is the same shape as the failure round 2 had to find by hand: .rise used animation-fill-mode: both and killed every hover and press on the surface while the assertion meant to catch it grepped the stylesheet and passed. If the settled override broke — a renamed attribute, a specificity change, a keyframe with a fill that outranks it — this gate would stay green and every frame this lab publishes would quietly become a photograph of a moment rather than of the work.
findings.fix: Measure at load rather than after it, and make the measurement provably able to fail. For this one check, bypass open()'s 1800ms wait: goto ?state=full&v=light and, inside the first animation frame after load, assert the first .bar is already at its data height (>= 60px at 1440x960); then goto ?state=full&v=light&motion=play and, at the same instant, assert the same bar measures <= 1px. Leave the attribute check at line 507 as it is.
findings.assertion: "settled is at height in frame one, and play is not": with ?state=full&v=light read within 100ms of load, document.querySelector('.bar').getBoundingClientRect().height >= 60; with ?state=full&v=light&motion=play read within 100ms of load, the same height <= 1.

findings.element: The ages card's spoken summary — the .sr line in strip(), lately.html:851, which prints `${j.age} days` for every job
findings.problem: Every other age on this surface goes through plural(): the mark's own accessible name says 'open 1 day' and its tooltip says '1 day open'. This one line hard-codes 'days'. Driven at 1440x960: ?state=quiet speaks 'Order tonic and the good olives, 1 days'; ?state=first-run speaks it three times — 'Confirm the Harbour wall cordon with the harbourmaster, 1 days; Order tonic and the good olives, 1 days; Send the midweek rate to the June 2027 couple, 1 days'. The full state hides it only because its youngest job happens to be two days old.
findings.consequence: In the one channel where this surface is nothing but its copy, the voice breaks concord on the simplest number in it, in two of the seven states — and does it a tab-press away from a mark that gets 'open 1 day' right, so the same fact is spoken two ways inside one card. Round 1 closed exactly this class for the KPI row (count-of-one-takes-a-plural-verb); this string was never inside that fix, and it is the last one left.
findings.assertion: For every state in full, partial, quiet and first-run, no .sr text matches /\b1 days\b/; and in ?state=first-run the ages card's .sr contains '1 day;' at least once.

findings.element: The overdue KPI card's word pair — lately.html:866, word: { one: "is past the day it was due", many: "past the day they were due" }
findings.problem: The row's other three pairs carry a finite verb in both numbers: hasn't/haven't moved, has/have nobody's name, is/are waiting. This one does not — the singular carries 'is' and the plural drops it. The plural is the branch that paints, so the row reads down as '3 haven't moved in a fortnight / 2 past the day they were due / 1 has nobody's name on it / 0 are waiting on something else': three sentences and one fragment. It carries into the card's accessible name too — '2 jobs past the day they were due, of 9 jobs open' beside '3 jobs haven't moved in a fortnight, of 9 jobs open' — and it means one card changes grammatical class with its own count while its three neighbours do not. Nothing was bought by dropping it: measured at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440, setting the string to 'are past the day they were due' leaves the word block's height and the card's height unchanged to the pixel at every width.
findings.consequence: The row is a four-item parallel and the eye reads the break before it reads the reason; the card carrying the most urgent category is the one that reads as an unfinished sentence. On a surface whose whole claim is that every string was chosen, the one string that was not is the one a reader catches.
findings.fix: In lately.html:866 set many: "are past the day they were due".
findings.assertion: Every non-lead KPI card's visible word block matches /^(is|are|has|have|hasn.t|haven.t)\b/ when rendered at ?state=full, and both branches of every word pair passed to kpi() match the same pattern when read from source.

findings.element: The coverage strip's Lab stamp — lately.html:955, Lab counts and ages are lab-authored
findings.problem: The strip is six key/value stamps set in tracked uppercase mono, where key and value are separated only by ink (--ink-2 against --ink-3), so each stamp reads as a single run. Five are key plus value: TASKS ANSWERED, TIMELINE ANSWERED, NOTES ANSWERED FOR YOU, READ 09:14 THURSDAY 16 JULY 2026, BOUND WORKSPACE OWNER READING DATE AND THE 9. The sixth reads LAB COUNTS AND AGES ARE LAB-AUTHORED — a sentence that restates its own key, and the only value in the row that is a sentence rather than a list. It sits directly beside BOUND, its matched half, whose value is a bare list of the same kind of thing.
findings.consequence: The one line whose entire job is to state provenance without ornament is the only line that stutters, at the size where every character is doing work; and the pair that should read as one decision — what is bound, what is not — reads as two different kinds of statement.
findings.fix: In lately.html:955 set the span to Lab counts and ages, so it stands parallel with Bound workspace, owner, reading date and the ${D.open}. interaction-check.mjs:267 tests the literal /lab-authored/ against the strip's text; change that clause to /counts and ages/, which is the property it was reaching for.
findings.assertion: The coverage strip's Lab stamp contains the substring 'lab' exactly once, case-insensitive; and the strip's text still matches all of /Tasks/, /Timeline/, /Notes/, /counts and ages/, /Bound/ and /reading date/.

biggestWin: Close the loading leak. One declaration — user-select: none on .sk-wrap — and the state stops handing over a reading it says it has not made, which is the only place on this surface where the honest-degradation contract is currently breached rather than kept. Everything else I found is a word: '1 days' becomes '1 day', 'past' becomes 'are past', and the Lab stamp stops repeating itself. Together that is under an hour of copy work — polish, not a build and not a different decision. What earned the 9.1 is the writing itself: three movement headings that name what a venue owner actually wants to know, a refusals movement almost nobody ships, degraded states written rather than templated, and a palette that is spent rather than merely obeyed — one indigo doing three declared jobs against an ink ramp, with status carried by shape and density so the four categories survive a reader who cannot separate red from amber. What holds it under 9.5 is that a studio's last read-through catches '1 days' and a missing verb, and this one did not.
